appraisal_events.evidence: "Ses traits m'étaient devenus courants, chargés d'un sens médiocre... ne ressemblaient plus en rien à ces caractères bizarres, intolérables que son visage m'avait présentés ce premier jour"; "la personnalité insignifiante et polie dont il n'était que la caricature, hideuse et sommaire."
appraisal_events.explanation: Habituation has stripped the director of his earlier grotesque, intolerable strangeness (disgust is now gone), but the settled result is a description of him as insignificant and merely a crude caricature of that earlier impression, a net downward reframing of his stature.

appraisal_events.evidence: "la petite Simonet devait être la plus jolie de toutes... celle... qui aurait pu devenir ma maîtresse, car elle était la seule qui... avait paru prendre conscience de mon fixe regard"; her name becomes "le premier vocable que nous retrouvions... presque avant le mot «je», comme si l'être qu'il nomme était plus nous que nous-même"; overheard gossip treats being her friend as a coveted "privilège".
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's expanding desire elevates la petite Simonet (Albertine) into a uniquely significant figure - deemed the prettiest of the group and singled out as receptive to his gaze - while local social gossip also frames friendship with her as an enviable privilege.

status_effects.explanation: His local stature is reduced from a once-intolerable, bizarre figure to a merely insignificant, banal caricature, even as personal disgust toward him fades.
She is singled out among the group of girls as the prettiest and as uniquely responsive to the narrator's attention, and her name takes on near-identity-defining significance in his imagination.
Overheard gossip on the promenade treats friendship with 'la petite Simonet' as a coveted privilege that draws others' curious attention, marking her as a locally desirable social reference point.

ambiguities: The directeur's shift in the narrator's perception is genuinely mixed: personal disgust fades even as he is redescribed as insignificant and a crude caricature, so the movement could be read as improvement, diminishment, or both.
